turns.query: I need in vitro to in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) for hepatic clearance for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs. I want predicted CLh (hepatic clearance mL/min/kg) and extraction ratio for each compound.
turns.responseText:
IVIVE Hepatic Clearance — Scales in vitro microsomal CLint to predicted human hepatic clearance for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs using well-stirred and parallel-tube models.

Input: Compound data CSV with 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs (compound_id / CLint_uL_per_min_mg / molecular_weight columns)
Key steps:

PKNCA + well-stirred & parallel-tube models → CLint_microsomal scaled to CLhep (mL/min/kg)
Hepatic extraction ratio (EH) computed per compound → classified as low / intermediate / high extraction


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh mL/min/kg + EH per compound) + clearance_summary.json (model comparison + scaling factors)

Decision gate: EH > 0.7 = high extraction (first-pass dominated, dose-sensitive); EH < 0.3 = low extraction (protein-binding sensitive) — flags which TKIs carry highest metabolic liability risk for lead prioritization.

turns.responseText:
IVIVE Hepatic Clearance — BCR-ABL1 TKI Panel — Scales measured microsomal CLint to predicted human hepatic clearance (CLh) and extraction ratio (EH) for 4 TKIs using the well-stirred liver model.

Input: 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs — Dasatinib (CLint=220, fu_plasma=0.04), Bosutinib (CLint=60, fu_plasma=0.03), Imatinib (CLint=25, fu_plasma=0.04), Nilotinib (CLint=12, fu_plasma=0.01); Qh=20.7 mL/min/kg, fu_mic=1.0
Key steps:

CLint scaling (microsomal protein × liver weight factors) → intrinsic CLint per compound
Well-stirred model: CLh = Qh × (fu_plasma × CLint_scaled) / (Qh + fu_plasma × CLint_scaled) → CLh (mL/min/kg) + EH per compound


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh mL/min/kg + EH per compound, ranked by metabolic liability) + clearance_summary.json (scaling factors, model parameters, compound-level flags)

Decision gate: EH > 0.7 = high extraction (Dasatinib expected) → first-pass dominated, high dose-sensitivity risk; EH < 0.3 = low extraction (Nilotinib expected) → protein-binding sensitive, safer metabolic profile for lead advancement.

Pocket Detection & Druggability Assessment — BCR-ABL1 (1IEP) — Identifies and ranks all binding pockets on the BCR-ABL1 DFG-out kinase structure using fpocket, with focus on the imatinib allosteric site.


Input: PDB ID 1IEP (BCR-ABL1 kinase, DFG-out conformation, imatinib-bound)


Key steps:

Fetch & validate PDB 1IEP → cleaned structure file ready for pocket detection
fpocket → per-pocket druggability scores, volumes, hydrophobicity, and alpha-sphere density across all detected cavities
Rank & filter top 10 pockets by druggability score + volume → annotated pocket summary



Expected output: pocket_summary.csv (top 10 pockets ranked by druggability score + volume) · druggability_scores.json (raw fpocket metrics per pocket) · ranked HTML report with 3D pocket visualization overlaid on 1IEP structure


Decision gate: Imatinib binding site (DFG-out allosteric pocket) should rank #1 with fpocket druggability score > 0.5 and volume > 400 Å³ — pockets below this threshold are unlikely to support high-affinity small-molecule binding.

turns.responseText:
BCR-ABL1 Campaign Safety-Potency Ranking — Ingests dual-assay IC50 data for 15 compounds and produces a composite score ranking potency against BCR-ABL1 kinase alongside hERG cardiac safety.

Input: 30-row assay CSV (15 compounds × 2 assay types: IC50_BCR_ABL1 in nM + hERG_IC50 in µM, dated 2026-03-15)
Key steps:

CSV parser → normalizes units, pivots to wide format, flags hERG risk tier (HIGH: < 1 µM, MODERATE: 1–10 µM, LOW: > 10 µM)
Composite scorer → log-transforms IC50 values, applies weighted rank (BCR-ABL1 potency 60% / hERG safety 40%), computes selectivity window (hERG IC50 ÷ BCR-ABL1 IC50)
Report generator → ranked compound table + HTML dashboard with potency-safety scatter plot


Expected output: ranked_compounds.csv (composite score, individual ranks, hERG risk tier, selectivity ratio) + HTML report (interactive scatter plot) + ranking_summary.json (top hits + flagged compounds)

Decision gate: Promote compounds with BCR-ABL1 IC50 < 10 nM AND hERG IC50 > 10 µM (selectivity window > 1,000×). CPD009 (hERG 0.08 µM) and CPD010 (hERG 0.05 µM) are auto-flagged as HIGH cardiac risk and will rank last regardless of BCR-ABL1 potency.

hERG safety gate (RDKit + hERG model) → flag any compound with hERG IC50 ≤ 1 μM as cardiac-unsafe and block from export
WuXi AppTec column formatter → maps compound_id, SMILES, IC50_nM, hERG_IC50_uM, composite_score to CRO-standard schema + computes MW/LogP via RDKit
CSV export → generates wuxiapptec_submission.csv + metadata JSON with campaign provenance



Expected output: wuxiapptec_submission.csv (WuXi-formatted, 5 compounds if all pass cardiac gate), submission_metadata.json (compound count, safety flags, export timestamp, campaign ID), and a rejection log if any compound fails hERG screening


Decision gate: All 5 compounds must clear hERG IC50 > 1 μM — any compound failing this threshold is automatically excluded from the CRO export and logged in the rejection report before submission.
